decisionsForDave: D2 — What art supports orbit? Unlocks the renderer and asset contract: A) Stylized dimensional 3D, following the supplied venue references. Medium art scope; readable forms and free yaw B) More realistic 3D. High art, lighting and device cost; greater visual detail C) Illustrated directional sprites. More paintings and limited tilt; continuous movement can expose mismatched facings Recommended: A. OPEN.

D3 — How deep should the crowd simulation go? Defines CPU, save and gameplay scope: A) Aggregate queues/services, animated representative people. Medium effort; visible behavior explains real totals B) Every attendee simulated and routed. High effort; individual stories, larger determinism/performance burden C) Decorative crowd only. Low effort; stronger atmosphere but no service explanation Recommended: A. OPEN.

D4 — How should Select and deletion behave? Unlocks the remaining Build interaction change: A) Select tool; Escape cancels placement; single removal uses undo; bulk Clear asks once. Medium UI work; few interruptions B) Confirm every removal, including single objects. More interruption; fewer immediate mistakes C) Keep current tools and undo only. No new interaction scope; accidental placement remains possible Recommended: A. OPEN.

D5 — How is performance accepted? Replaces the ambiguous headless 16ms target only if selected: A) Stable CI regression scenes plus real-device targets: proposed 60fps desktop / 30fps low-power tier. Thresholds fixed after baselines B) Require 60fps on every supported device. High optimization cost and stricter hardware scope C) Keep current absolute headless p95 <16ms gate. Lowest specification effort; unreliable across software-rendered runners Recommended: A. OPEN.

D6 — Research scope, CT-DEC-13: A) Three-project Lot pilot after live services are measurable: Patch standards, Service training, Admission lanes B) Implement the same pilot before live services, against current outcomes; more rework risk C) Defer all research; leave CT-DEC-13 Proposed Recommended: A. OPEN.

D7 — Ownership and economy scope: A) Keep rentals for the first live-show slice; add ownership afterward B) Ownership and ledger first. More persistent business depth, larger save and accounting work C) Rentals only for this release; no ownership milestone Recommended: A. OPEN.

D8 — Existing sprite library: A) Inventory provenance now; retain during prototype; archive unused art once replacements are accepted B) Keep every asset as a permanent library. Lowest transition risk, ongoing size/style debt C) Commission or regenerate all art immediately. Highest cost before renderer dimensions are proven Recommended: A. OPEN.

D9 — CT-DEC-10 Lot economy and progression: A) Keep current numbers experimental; conduct paired strategy tests and a human career before accepting B) Accept the present Lot goals and deal/relationship rules now; fun still needs testing C) Prioritize retuning first: make PA/lights situationally worthwhile and compare door/guarantee strategies before expansion Recommended: A. OPEN.

D10 — CT-DEC-11 later rooms: A) Keep implemented room behavior experimental while venue art and tier-specific tests develop B) Accept current behavior: grid Club, returnable Lot, house rigs, seated multi-night shell, two-stage grounds C) Reopen room mechanics before art: specify fixed-room versus grid behavior and future stage scheduling first Recommended: A. OPEN.

D11 — When may the game be promoted publicly?: A) Wait for the 3D Lot and live-operations pilot plus existing release gates B) Promote the current playable once existing provenance, design and human acceptance gates pass; label it early access C) Keep it unlisted without a launch milestone for now Recommended: A. OPEN.
